newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho ruling party torn over leadership row.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho ruling party torn over leadership row.

text.p: A rift between Lesotho's ruling Basotoland Congress Party (BCP) and its leader-cum-prime minister deepened on Thursday as senior party members accused him of trying to remove them from office.
The party's secretary general Godfrey Kolisang told a news conference on Thursday that Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle had unilaterally called a meeting of 650 constituency members at the weekend.

"The intention is to destabilise the party, because he (Mokhehle) realises that the party as a whole is dissatisfied with his leadership and is therefore being confrontational and provocative," Kolisang said in a party statement to reporters.
BCP deputy leader Molapo Qhobela cautioned that if there was a plan to remove the party's national executive from office at the weekend, "somebody will end up with a bloody nose".
"I hope such madness will not take place," he told reporters.

Tensions between the BCP leader and his national executive were taken to the Lesotho High Court earlier this year after the party's executive committee voted to expel Mokhehle as leader on the grounds that he did not cooperate in the running of party affairs.
The High Court ordered the BCP to call a general meeting to democratically elect a new leader and executive committee.
A meeting has been scheduled for July 26, but Mokhehle has said he will not attend unless it is held at his residence, because he fears for his life.
Mokhehle is one of the founder members of the 45-year-old BCP, which won Lesotho's first democratic elections in two decades in March 1993. He has not reacted to his party's allegations.
Lesotho is a small mountainous kingdom surrounded by and reliant on regional economic giant South Africa. It is often hit by crises, including army mutinies and police strikes.
